Battle of Hat Dich.fact: On 6 February 1969, two additional battalions from the Thủ Đức VC Regiment were reported to have entered the Hat Dich area and 4 RAR/NZ (ANZAC) which consisted of three Australian and two New Zealand companies, was subsequently redeployed with tanks and armoured personnel carriers in support, resulting in the heaviest contacts of the operation.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Greville subsequently establish FSB Janice in the rice fields at the northern end of the _____
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Greville subsequently establish FSB Janice in the rice fields at the northern end of the Rung Sat. Overnight Australian cavalry from 3 Troop had been deployed in a night ambush 3 kilometres (1.9 mi) west of Phu My, adjacent to Route 15 on the edge of the Rung Sat.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: A number of successful ambushes were conducted by the Australian and _____ infantry over the coming days, while patrolling by day resulted in the discovery of a number of large weapons caches
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: 4 RAR/NZ subsequently occupied a battalion defensive position at FSB Sandpiper, and once set up the rifle companies began a patrolling and ambushing program. The requirement to be redeployed at short notice prevented the Australians from operating any more than one hour from Sandpiper however, and this constraint also limited their effectiveness in preventing interdiction along Route 15.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Overnight Australian cavalry from 3 Troop had been deployed in a night ambush _____ (1.9 mi) west of Phu My, adjacent to Route 15 on the edge of the Rung Sat
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Overnight Australian cavalry from 3 Troop had been deployed in a night ambush 3 kilometres (1.9 mi) west of Phu My, adjacent to Route 15 on the edge of the Rung Sat.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: A motorised junk and a sampan were subsequently sunk and three VC killed by the _____
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: A motorised junk and a sampan were subsequently sunk and three VC killed by the Australians. Heavy fighting ensured with the action lasting five hours as the Australians called in mortar and artillery fire, and were also supported by air strikes and helicopter light fire teams.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Heavy fighting ensured with the action lasting five hours as the _____ called in mortar and artillery fire, and were also supported by air strikes and helicopter light fire teams
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: A motorised junk and a sampan were subsequently sunk and three VC killed by the Australians. Heavy fighting ensured with the action lasting five hours as the Australians called in mortar and artillery fire, and were also supported by air strikes and helicopter light fire teams.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: The lead _____ platoon—12 Platoon—had suffered one wounded during the initial contact, and a further five were wounded as the sweep continued
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: A motorised junk and a sampan were subsequently sunk and three VC killed by the Australians. Heavy fighting ensured with the action lasting five hours as the Australians called in mortar and artillery fire, and were also supported by air strikes and helicopter light fire teams.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: On 8 _____, D Company 9 RAR was engaged in the north-east of their AO with RPGs and small arms by a platoon-size force in a bunker system
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: On 8 February, D Company 9 RAR was engaged in the north-east of their AO with RPGs and small arms by a platoon-size force in a bunker system.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Due to the heavy fire the evacuation of the wounded was delayed, and the _____ helicopter was forced to depart without the casualties, one of whom subsequently died of his wounds
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Due to the heavy fire the evacuation of the wounded was delayed, and the Dustoff helicopter was forced to depart without the casualties, one of whom subsequently died of his wounds.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Later during the subsequent follow-up over the next two days, the _____ found an extensive complex of four bunker systems with a total of over 60 mutually supporting bunkers
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: A number of VC snipers in trees had also engaged the Australians, in conjunction with the troops in the bunkers and the area was subsequently bombarded by the Australians with artillery, helicopter light fire teams and air strikes before 12 Platoon was able to break contact. Later during the subsequent follow-up over the next two days, the Australians found an extensive complex of four bunker systems with a total of over 60 mutually supporting bunkers.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: At last light in _____, 3 Platoon V Company 4 RAR/NZ observed around 35 VC moving west out of the area of operations and they were engaged by artillery and helicopter light fire teams
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At last light in AO Tiki, 3 Platoon V Company 4 RAR/NZ observed around 35 VC moving west out of the area of operations and they were engaged by artillery and helicopter light fire teams.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: The following day the _____ conducted a sweep of the area and recovered one body
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: The following day the New Zealanders conducted a sweep of the area and recovered one body. The following day, 9 February, contacts continued between the New Zealanders and the VC.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Meanwhile, the ARVN 52nd _____ concluded operations in AO Moose and commenced operations in AO Warragul
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Meanwhile, the ARVN 52nd Regiment concluded operations in AO Moose and commenced operations in AO Warragul.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: The following day, 9 _____, contacts continued between the New Zealanders and the VC
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: The following day, 9 February, contacts continued between the New Zealanders and the VC.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: At 14:38 a section patrol from 2 Platoon W Company 4 RAR/NZ clashing with five VC at _____ (33 ft) while conducting a reconnaissance of a track, killing two and capturing an AK-47 and a pistol
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At 14:38 a section patrol from 2 Platoon W Company 4 RAR/NZ clashing with five VC at 10 metres (33 ft) while conducting a reconnaissance of a track, killing two and capturing an AK-47 and a pistol.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: A follow-up sweep by 2 _____ located a small camp and five packs
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At 14:38 a section patrol from 2 Platoon W Company 4 RAR/NZ clashing with five VC at 10 metres (33 ft) while conducting a reconnaissance of a track, killing two and capturing an AK-47 and a pistol. A follow-up sweep by 2 Platoon located a small camp and five packs.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Further fleeting contacts occurred during the afternoon and early evening, before V _____ sighted 10 VC at 19:50 from their night position and subsequently engaged them with artillery
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At 14:38 a section patrol from 2 Platoon W Company 4 RAR/NZ clashing with five VC at 10 metres (33 ft) while conducting a reconnaissance of a track, killing two and capturing an AK-47 and a pistol. Further fleeting contacts occurred during the afternoon and early evening, before V Company sighted 10 VC at 19:50 from their night position and subsequently engaged them with artillery.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: At first light the next morning the _____ were contacted while checking the area of the previous night's engagement and one VC was killed
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At first light the next morning the New Zealanders were contacted while checking the area of the previous night's engagement and one VC was killed. The VC subsequently withdrew carrying two bodies, while a sweep early the next morning resulted in the New Zealanders capturing a pack containing four pistols and three AK-47 magazines.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: The VC subsequently withdrew carrying two bodies, while a sweep early the next morning resulted in the _____ capturing a pack containing four pistols and three AK-47 magazines
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At first light the next morning the New Zealanders were contacted while checking the area of the previous night's engagement and one VC was killed. The VC subsequently withdrew carrying two bodies, while a sweep early the next morning resulted in the New Zealanders capturing a pack containing four pistols and three AK-47 magazines.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: That evening V _____ again observed 14 VC moving through their area of operations and they again directed artillery onto them
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Further fleeting contacts occurred during the afternoon and early evening, before V Company sighted 10 VC at 19:50 from their night position and subsequently engaged them with artillery. That evening V Company again observed 14 VC moving through their area of operations and they again directed artillery onto them.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Later, during a search in _____ on the afternoon of 14 February, C Company 9 RAR contacted a strong VC force in a large bunker system
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Later, during a search in AO Wondai on the afternoon of 14 February, C Company 9 RAR contacted a strong VC force in a large bunker system.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: In AO Tiki, D _____ 4 RAR/NZ mounted a series of ambushes on the creeks which flowed into the Rung Sat
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: The following day A Company was deployed with tanks to assist a further assault by C Company in the bunker system, which was again found to have been abandoned by the VC after having suffered a number of casualties. In AO Tiki, D Company 4 RAR/NZ mounted a series of ambushes on the creeks which flowed into the Rung Sat.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: On 15 _____ 10 Platoon D Company had deployed to southern end of the battalion AO to mount a night ambush on a high bank on a sharp bend in the Suoi Cau river
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: On 15 February 10 Platoon D Company had deployed to southern end of the battalion AO to mount a night ambush on a high bank on a sharp bend in the Suoi Cau river.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: The infantry were reinforced by 90 mm M67 recoilless rifles (RCLs) from the _____, which were placed on the flanks
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: The infantry were reinforced by 90 mm M67 recoilless rifles (RCLs) from the Tracker Platoon, which were placed on the flanks.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: At least two sampans were sunk and six VC killed before they were able to withdraw to the southern bank and engage the _____ with small arms and RPGs
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At least two sampans were sunk and six VC killed before they were able to withdraw to the southern bank and engage the Australians with small arms and RPGs. At first light the next morning the Australians swept the area, wading through the shallow river at low tide, subsequently locating another damaged sampan, an AK-47, an RPG-2 and two RPG rounds.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: At first light the next morning the Australians swept the area, wading through the shallow river at low tide, subsequently locating another damaged sampan, an AK-_____, an RPG-2 and two RPG rounds
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At 14:38 a section patrol from 2 Platoon W Company 4 RAR/NZ clashing with five VC at 10 metres (33 ft) while conducting a reconnaissance of a track, killing two and capturing an AK-47 and a pistol. The VC subsequently withdrew carrying two bodies, while a sweep early the next morning resulted in the New Zealanders capturing a pack containing four pistols and three AK-47 magazines.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: B and W _____ 4 RAR/NZ, each accompanied by a tracker team and a Centurion tank troop from B Squadron, 1st Armoured Regiment were subsequently tasked to patrol to the area by separate routes
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: B and W Companies 4 RAR/NZ, each accompanied by a tracker team and a Centurion tank troop from B Squadron, 1st Armoured Regiment were subsequently tasked to patrol to the area by separate routes.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Well concealed in bunkers the defenders successfully initiated a command-detonated directional mine and opened fire with small-arms and RPGs, killing one _____ and wounding five others
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: On 16 February, just prior to a ceasefire for the Tết New Year festival, the Australian command had received information from an agent about the location of large weapon caches in the north of AO Tiki, and a large VC force was also expected to be in position. Well concealed in bunkers the defenders successfully initiated a command-detonated directional mine and opened fire with small-arms and RPGs, killing one Australian and wounding five others.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: The remainder of the casualties were then moved by helicopter to the _____ at Vung Tau
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: The remainder of the casualties were then moved by helicopter to the Australian Field Hospital at Vung Tau.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: A number of air strikes were also directed onto the position, while _____ planned an attack to destroy the VC force
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: A number of air strikes were also directed onto the position, while Reynolds planned an attack to destroy the VC force.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Gradually B _____ gained the upper hand and prepared to assault the position, returning heavy fire with small arms while the tanks continued to engage the bunkers from close range
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Gradually B Company gained the upper hand and prepared to assault the position, returning heavy fire with small arms while the tanks continued to engage the bunkers from close range.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Lacking the medium artillery and air strikes required to successfully assault the fortified position, B _____ withdrew to a safe distance and kept the position under observation and fire
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Lacking the medium artillery and air strikes required to successfully assault the fortified position, B Company withdrew to a safe distance and kept the position under observation and fire.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: A follow-up attack schedule for the next day was also cancelled due to the unavailability of _____ artillery
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Circling overhead in another Sioux helicopter Greville protested, and although Pearson had supported him the Americans refused to provide offensive support despite the contact having been initiated by the VC. A follow-up attack schedule for the next day was also cancelled due to the unavailability of American artillery.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: During the night a large VC force was observed withdrawing, with one party of about 30 men passing close to a concealed _____; frustrated, the Australians observed the truce and held their fire
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: During the night a large VC force was observed withdrawing, with one party of about 30 men passing close to a concealed Centurion; frustrated, the Australians observed the truce and held their fire.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: A thorough search of the area by the _____ was not possible however, and B Company was ordered to return to their patrol area to prepare for redeployment
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Although there were numerous signs of casualties, with a large number of blood trails and some damaged weapons the Australians found only three dead, with the VC once again having cleared the battlefield of the dead and wounded during the night. Later intelligence suggested that the position had been occupied by the headquarters of the 274th Regiment and one of its battalions and the Australians considered it likely that the VC battalion had fought a delaying action to allow the headquarters ...

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: The fighting had been one of the more significant actions of _____ and for his leadership during this action Reynolds was awarded the Military Cross
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: The fighting had been one of the more significant actions of Operation Goodwood and for his leadership during this action Reynolds was awarded the Military Cross.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: At 01:45 on 18 _____ a sentry from D Company had detected noise and movement to the south, just outside the wire
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At 01:45 on 18 February a sentry from D Company had detected noise and movement to the south, just outside the wire.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Estimated at up to company strength, the VC were observed clearly through a _____ scope and were moving noisily, likely unaware of their proximity to the fire support base
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Estimated at up to company strength, the VC were observed clearly through a Starlight scope and were moving noisily, likely unaware of their proximity to the fire support base.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Later, in response to the upcoming communist offensive _____ also warned Greville to be prepared to move 4 RAR/NZ further north to help defend Long Binh and Biên Hòa
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Later, in response to the upcoming communist offensive Pearson also warned Greville to be prepared to move 4 RAR/NZ further north to help defend Long Binh and Biên Hòa.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: FSB _____ closed and HQ 1 ATF moved to FSB Kerry in preparation for upcoming operations
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: FSB Julia closed and HQ 1 ATF moved to FSB Kerry in preparation for upcoming operations.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Throughout the operation the bulk of the contacts had been initiated by the _____, a reverse of the American trend in which more than two-thirds of actions were normally initiated by the VC
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Throughout the operation the bulk of the contacts had been initiated by the Australians, a reverse of the American trend in which more than two-thirds of actions were normally initiated by the VC. Although there were few major actions, the operation was considered a success by the Australians and following it VC activity in 1 ATFs area of operations visibly lessened as the VC were forced to abandon their permanent bases in the Hat Dich and disrupting their preparations for upcoming offensive ...

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: From _____ most operations tended to be platoon and company-sized, and confined to Phước Tuy
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: From 1969 most operations tended to be platoon and company-sized, and confined to Phước Tuy.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: There was little respite for the _____ though, with both 4 RAR/NZ and 9 RAR immediately redeploying in anticipation of another PAVN/VC offensive during Tet, under Operation Federal
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Operation Goodwood was one of the longest out of province operations mounted by the Australians during the war and was also the last Australian multi-battalion operation to be fought across the border with third-country forces. It had been a period of intense activity for the Australians and the Royal Australian Regiment, the 3rd Cavalry Regiment and 1st Armoured Regiment were subsequently awarded the battle honour "Hat Dich", one of only five presented to Australian units during the war.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: 1 RAR subsequently returned to Australia after being relieved by 5 RAR—under the command of _____—on 15 February
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: 1 RAR subsequently returned to Australia after being relieved by 5 RAR—under the command of Lieutenant Colonel Colin Kahn—on 15 February.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Arriving in Sydney on 28 February _____, 1 RAR was welcomed home with a march through the city
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: This operation in late-February 1969 saw 1 ATF—less one battalion and other elements required to secure its base in Nui Dat—once again operating outside Phước Tuy Province to secure the major bases of Long Binh, Biên Hòa and the capital Saigon from an impending offensive. Arriving in Sydney on 28 February 1969, 1 RAR was welcomed home with a march through the city.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: During the tour—its second in South Vietnam—the battalion had killed at least _____ VC and destroyed a large number of bunkers, camps, and caches and had been heavily involved in the Battle of Coral–B
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: During the tour—its second in South Vietnam—the battalion had killed at least 276 VC and destroyed a large number of bunkers, camps, and caches and had been heavily involved in the Battle of Coral–Balmoral.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: The _____ Tet offensive began in the early hours of 23 February, with PAVN/VC attacks against US and ARVN installations and district capitals
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Arriving in Sydney on 28 February 1969, 1 RAR was welcomed home with a march through the city. The 1969 Tet offensive began in the early hours of 23 February, with PAVN/VC attacks against US and ARVN installations and district capitals.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Lacking the ferocity of the _____ Tet Offensive, the outburst soon slackened, however
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Lacking the ferocity of the 1968 Tet Offensive, the outburst soon slackened, however.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: In III CTZ, where 1 ATF operated, over a period of five days there were 175 attacks by fire and just 15 ground assaults, while the _____/VC suffered over 1,800 killed and 320 captured
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: The 1969 Tet offensive began in the early hours of 23 February, with PAVN/VC attacks against US and ARVN installations and district capitals. In III CTZ, where 1 ATF operated, over a period of five days there were 175 attacks by fire and just 15 ground assaults, while the PAVN/VC suffered over 1,800 killed and 320 captured.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Although _____ forces were by now operating in these areas, VC guerrilla groups operated with freedom, especially at night
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Although ARVN forces were by now operating in these areas, VC guerrilla groups operated with freedom, especially at night.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: As a consequence Australian operations in mid-_____ were forced to focus on the area around Dat Do and the Long Hải Hills, as they attempted to restrict the VC's access to the local population
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Regardless, with the bulk of 1 ATF operating away from Nui Dat in first half of 1969, the VC again became active in the populated central and southern areas of Phước Tuy Province, including Dat Do and Long Dien and the villages between Dat Do and the coast. As a consequence Australian operations in mid-1969 were forced to focus on the area around Dat Do and the Long Hải Hills, as they attempted to restrict the VC's access to the local population.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Later, on 6–7 June _____ the Australians were engaged in fierce close-quarter house-to-house fighting with PAVN/VC forces during the Battle of Binh Ba
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Regardless, with the bulk of 1 ATF operating away from Nui Dat in first half of 1969, the VC again became active in the populated central and southern areas of Phước Tuy Province, including Dat Do and Long Dien and the villages between Dat Do and the coast. As a consequence Australian operations in mid-1969 were forced to focus on the area around Dat Do and the Long Hải Hills, as they attempted to restrict the VC's access to the local population.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Regardless, D _____ deployed by APC and secured FSB Sandpiper, 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) east of Route 15, while the remainder of the battalion deployed by road
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Regardless, D Company deployed by APC and secured FSB Sandpiper, 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) east of Route 15, while the remainder of the battalion deployed by road.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: An assault by the _____ platoon pushed the VC out of the bunkers and they secured the area after following the withdrawing force 200 metres (220 yd) to the south-west
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At 17:00 7 Platoon contacted 14 VC armed with AK-47 assault rifles on the edge of a clearing, killing one while the others withdrew to a bunker system and engaged the Australians with small arms and 60 mm mortars. An assault by the Australian platoon pushed the VC out of the bunkers and they secured the area after following the withdrawing force 200 metres (220 yd) to the south-west.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Also that evening, elements of 2 Troop, A Squadron, 3rd _____ had been occupying an ambush site on a track 2.5 kilometres (1.6 mi) west of Route 15, northeast of Phu My in Phước Tuy Province
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Also that evening, elements of 2 Troop, A Squadron, 3rd Cavalry Regiment had been occupying an ambush site on a track 2.5 kilometres (1.6 mi) west of Route 15, northeast of Phu My in Phước Tuy Province.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: More than 1,000 metres (1,100 yd) away, Honner moved quickly to bring the remainder of C _____ to the aid of the platoon in contact
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: That morning in AO Wondai, 1 Platoon A Company 1 RAR was watching the northern bank of Suoi Cau Moi and at 07:45 they contacted three VC as they attempted to cross the creek, killing one. Thirty minutes later 7 Platoon, C Company had been engaged by two VC while moving into a new ambush location.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Meanwhile, a number of SAS patrols were inserted by air and road on 6 _____ 1969 to gather information on PAVN/VC troop movements
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Meanwhile, a number of SAS patrols were inserted by air and road on 6 January 1969 to gather information on PAVN/VC troop movements. Further patrols were deployed to the southern Biên Hòa-Firestone Trail area in mid-January, while additional SAS patrols were inserted on 29 January in an attempt to ascertain PAVN/VC troop movements.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: On 13 _____ moved to establish FSB Margaret 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) east of Tam Phuoc in Biên Hòa Province, located in AO Kilcoy immediately west of AO Wondai
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: On 13 January Bennett moved to establish FSB Margaret 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) east of Tam Phuoc in Biên Hòa Province, in AO Kilcoy immediately west of AO Wondai.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: At 06:15 the following morning an ambush by 4 _____ B Company contacted a group of five VC, killing one and wounding a second
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: At dusk an ambush from 6 Platoon B Company had engaged two VC, and although one soldier was seen to fall no casualties were found during the sweep. At 06:15 the following morning an ambush by 4 Platoon B Company contacted a group of five VC, killing one and wounding a second.

Battle of Hat Dich.subject: Indian Aviation & Shipping
Battle of Hat Dich.question: Three weeks later three graves were discovered 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) west of _____ and it was believed that they had also been killed during the 2 Troop ambush mounted on 19 January
Battle of Hat Dich.fact: The same evening 3 Troop mounted a successful ambush close to FSB Chestnut, killing one VC and wounding another three. Three weeks later three graves were discovered 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) west of FSB Chestnut and it was believed that they had also been killed during the 2 Troop ambush mounted on 19 January.

Battle of Hat Dich.fact: Meanwhile, in AO Wondai B Company 9 RAR subsequently conducted a number of successful ambushes and on 4 February 5 Platoon ambushed a VC party of eight men at first light, killing six of them.
